title: Micro-onboard heuristic canvas + 90min lab templates
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a compact, opinionated artifact for running a 60–90 minute micro-onboard lab for new SDK adopters (internal hires, pilot customers, or partner integrators). It pairs a friction-mapping heuristic canvas with ready-to-run sprint templates and telemetry checkpoints so the facilitator can run a consistent, measurable session in low-prep time.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- We keep iterating many similar onboarding sessions with inconsistent outcomes.
- Engineering-heavy sessions often skip telemetry agreement, so we can’t measure adoption lift or early breakage.
- Developers want a tiny success path (sample app -> first request -> instrumented telemetry) that fits into one meeting.

High-level outcomes (success criteria for the session):
1) Participant has a working sample app making a call to Redwood SDK with streaming enabled.
2) Quick telemetry is in place: 3 core events + an error counter, visible in the sandbox dashboard.
3) Team documents 1–2 friction points on the heuristic canvas and a next-step (owner + ticket).

Session formats (pick one):
- Lightning (60 minutes): quick install + run + telemetry + wrap. Best for internal hires.
- Workshop (90 minutes): same as Lightning but with paired debugging time and a short prompt quality check. Good for external pilots.
- Drop-in (30 minutes): demo + pointers; not recommended for telemetry goals.

Heuristic canvas (one page, facilitator copy) — 6 zones:
1) First-hit friction: install, auth, API key fidelity, env vars, quick token issues.
2) Latency expectations: local vs hosted model, streaming, SDK defaults that matter.
3) Error & retry surface: network errors, rate limit messages, model fallback signals.
4) Observability: which events matter (see telemetry section), logs, and sample dashboard queries.
5) UX lift: prompts + example failures (hallucination/formatting).
6) Next-step triggers: who will own follow-ups, deadlines, and gating for production.

Facilitator instructions (pre-run checklist):
- Confirm workspace provisioned with free trial credits or pilot token.
- Create a temporary repo with sample app and a README with a single-step run. (Repo template: SDK-mini-lab-starter)
- Pre-create two dashboard views: "Microlab / Live" and "Microlab / Errors" and share link in meeting chat.
- Ensure the meeting board (Miro/Google doc) has the canvas pasted and a blank ticket template.

90-minute lab template (timeline):
- 0:00–0:05 — Quick intro + outcomes + share artifacts.
- 0:05–0:20 — Environment & install (copy/paste flow). Helper: a 1-file sample app in Node or Python.
- 0:20–0:40 — Make the first call (streaming path) and validate response shape.
- 0:40–0:55 — Wire minimal telemetry (three events + error counter) and verify in dashboard.
- 0:55–1:15 — Paired debugging: surface 2 friction items and try one mitigation.
- 1:15–1:20 — Prompt quality checklist: run 3 prompt variants, capture differences.
- 1:20–1:30 — Canvas review + assign follow-ups + close.

Minimum runnable artifact (what participants should clone):
- README with 6 commands: clone, install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run, open dashboard link, inject a bad prompt to observe error.
- Single-file app (index.js or main.py) that:
  - Installs one sdk dependency,
  - Calls Redwood "chat.completions" (or text generation) with streaming enabled,
  - Prints tokens as they stream, and
  - Exposes a small /metrics endpoint (optional: for local scraping)

Telemetry contract (minimal) — events to emit during micro-onboard:
- event.sdk.start (attributes: runtime: node|python, sample: true, model: name)
- event.sdk.first_success (attributes: latency_ms, sequence_length, streamed: true|false)
- event.sdk.prompt_variant (attributes: variant_id, tokens_in, tokens_out)
- metric.sdk.errors.count (counter)
- tag user.provisioned: true|false (if running with a pilot token)

Recommended instrumentation snippets (pseudo):
- Node (tiny):
  logEvent('event.sdk.start', {runtime:'node', sample:true, model:'gptx-small'});
  const start = Date.now();
  // call sdk
  logEvent('event.sdk.first_success', {latency_ms: Date.now()-start, sequence_length: 64, streamed: true});

Why telemetry early matters:
- We can track drop-offs during install or at first request — useful to triage SDK bugs rapidly.
- Prompt variants give quick signal if defaults are miscalibrated for our model catalog.

Sample dashboard queries (for the Microlab / Live view):
- Last 24h: COUNT(event.sdk.start) by runtime
- P95 latency for event.sdk.first_success where streamed=true
- Errors: SUM(metric.sdk.errors.count) grouped by error_message

Common friction patterns and mitigations (collected heuristics):
- auth-error: participants mix up prod/test tokens. Mitigation: pre-populate a temporary token and instruct how to revoke.
- CORS/local proxy: browser samples fail. Mitigation: show quick local proxy pattern and recommend server-first dev flow.
- Streaming confusion: partial tokens printed then nothing. Mitigation: check SDK transport (ws/http) and model compatibility table.

Prompt quality check (2-minute recipe):
- Run baseline prompt (1-sentence), record tokens/outcome.
- Add guardrails: system prompt or schema output spec, run again.
- Record differences and capture a short note on hallucination/formatting.

Artifacts to produce at the end of the session:
- Filled heuristic canvas (photo or copy into board).
- 1 ticket per friction item (title, short reproduction steps, priority).
- A short bullet note (owner: ) capturing whether template app should be extended.

Follow-up play (owner checklist):
- Within 48 hours: convert highest-priority friction into a reproducible CI test or PR.
- Within 7 days: improve sample README and add a dedicated telemetry snippet.

Facilitator troubleshooting crib sheet (quick):
- "SDK install fails" — check node/python version, clear cache, re-run install with verbose flags.
- "No streaming" — verify model supports streaming; check client transport and firewall.
- "Dashboard empty" — ensure telemetry key maps to pilot account and events are being flushed (call flush() if library buffers).

Open questions / TODOs (session-maintained):
- Decide a canonical repo name and where it lives (GH org vs internal repo).
- Should the microlab include an offline/airgapped variant for Private customers? (low effort)
- Agreement on default model & prompt templates for the lab.

Appendix A — Quick sample prompts to use in lab:
- Baseline: "Summarize the text below in 2 sentences."
- Constrained: "Return a JSON object {title:..., bullets:[...]} with keys only."
- Safety test: "Classify whether the following text contains PII: <text>"

Appendix B — Minimal checklist for production handoff after a pilot:
- Ensure telemetry names match production naming conventions.
- Add feature flags for model selection and streaming toggles.
- Add canary rollouts + SLO for first-request latency.

Notes to self (Priya):
- Try this with the Solutions-eng pilot next week (Nov cohort).
- Capture a short Loom recording of the 90-minute flow and pin it to the repo README.

End of doc.
